name: Hiraizumi – Temples, Gardens and Archaeological Sites Representing the Buddhist Pure Land
description: In Iwate Prefecture in northern Japan, Hiraizumi was a thriving 11th- and 12th-century capital whose rulers rivaled Kyoto. Five sites survive, including temple remains, landscaped ponds and gardens, and sacred Mount Kinkeisan. Together they were laid out to evoke the Buddhist Pure Land, the paradise people hoped to reach after death, blending Buddhist ideas with older Japanese nature worship.
